reason: The cited evidence does not address the key premises. E1 mentions actively-learned MTPs for solid solution strengthening and ductility in refractory MPEAs, not fusion free energies or entropy. E2 describes a standard formation energy calculation, irrelevant to the hypothesis. E3 reports configurational and vibrational entropy from first-principles for CoCrFeNiTax, but does not involve active learning, MTPs, or fusion free energy calculations. No cited passage supports the claimed accuracy, speedup, or applicability of the proposed AL-MTP method for fusion thermodynamics.
premises: Active learning can train a moment tensor potential (MTP) on sparse ab initio MD snapshots for solid and liquid phases.
An MTP trained this way can accurately reproduce free energy differences and key entropy contributions (vibrational, anharmonic, electron-vibration) of fusion.
Using this MTP in enhanced sampling will reduce computational cost by ~10x vs. explicit ab initio MD and be faster than TOR-TILD.
The approach works for elemental, binary, and moderately complex high-entropy systems near the melting point.
